full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain, J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 25.01.2011 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 897 of 2008 discharging the Rule and affirming the judgment and decree 19.04.2006 passed by the learned Joint District Judge (In-Charge), First Court, Kushtia in Title Appeal No. 162 of 2004 (heard along with Title Appeal No. 253 of 2004) dismissing the appeals and affirming the judgment and decree dated 24.04.2004 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Khoksha, Kushtia in Title Suit No. 190 of 2001 decreeing the suit. 

 5. The trial Court upon hearing both the sides by the judgment and order dated 24.04.2004 decreed the suit. Against which, the defendants preferred Appeal No. 162 of 2004 and by a third-party preferred Title Appeal No. 253 of 2004 before the learned District Judge, Kushtia. On transfer, the appeals were heard and disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge (In-Charge), First Court, Kushtia, who by his judgment and order dated 19.04.2006 dismissed the appeals and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the appellate Court, the defendants moved the High Court Division by filing a revisional application and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 897 of 2008. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division upon hearing the parties by the judgment and order dated 25.01.2011 discharged the Rule and affirmed the judgment and decree of the Courts below. 

 8. Mr. Ekramul Haque, learned Deputy Attorney General, appearing on behalf of the leave-petitioners, submits that the suit land having been acquired by the Government for the purpose of Kushtia-Jhenaidah Road and full compensation money having been paid to the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff and the suit being absolutely illegal and misconceived and both the Courts below having decreed the suit on misconception of law, the High Court Division erred in law in discharging the Rule without considering those aspects and as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside.
